rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a pleasure voyage by cruise ship.

example.english: We’re going on a five-night cruise and will stay on the ship.
example.traditional: 我哋今次去郵輪旅行，會喺船上住五晚。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 ci3 heoi3 jau4 leon4 leoi5 hang4 wui5 hai2 syun4 soeng6 zyu6 ng5 maan5

rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose choice for saying that you go boating or sail around for pleasure.

example.english: We’re going to cruise on Sunday.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 sing1 kei4 jat6 heoi3 jau4 syun4 ho4

rows.note: Use this when someone wins easily and convincingly, especially in a match or competition.

example.english: We cruise to an easy win over our opponents this match.
example.traditional: 我哋隊波今場輕鬆咁贏咗對手。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 deoi6 bo1 gam1 coeng4 hing1 sung1 gam2 jeng4 zo2 deoi3 sau2

rows.note: Use this for an aircraft or ship travelling at an efficient, steady cruising speed.

example.english: The passenger plane will cruise at a constant speed.
example.traditional: 客機會以恆定速度巡航。
example.jyutping: haak3 gei1 wui5 ji5 hang4 ding6 cuk1 dou6 ceon4 hong4

rows.note: Use this technical noun for an aircraft’s level, constant-speed cruising phase.

example.english: After the aircraft enters the cruise phase, the captain tells everyone they may unfasten their seat belts.
example.traditional: 飛機進入巡航階段後，機長先通知大家可以解開安全帶。
example.jyutping: fei1 gei1 zeon3 jap6 ceon4 hong4 gaai1 dyun6 hau6 gei1 zoeng2 sin1 tung1 zi1 daai6 gaa1 ho2 ji5 gaai2 hoi1 on1 cyun4 daai2
